members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working:
Evaluate each statement:
(A) Colloidal particles pass through ordinary filter paper. Typical filter paper pores ~10 µm (10,000 nm), colloids 1–1000 nm, so particles can pass through; statement is generally correct.
(B) Brownian movement helps keep a sol stable against settling. True; Brownian motion prevents sedimentation.
(C) Colloidal particles range in size from about 1 nm to 1000 nm. Standard definition: 1 nm to 1 µm (1000 nm); correct.
(D) True solutions show a strong Tyndall effect. True solutions have molecules small enough that light scattering is negligible; they do not show a strong Tyndall effect. Hence statement D is NOT correct.
Thus the incorrect statement is option D.

events.stem:
Colloidal systems exhibit distinctive surface and thermodynamic characteristics.
Which one of the following statements about properties of colloids is correct?
(A) Colloidal particles are retained by ordinary filter paper.
(B) Lyophobic sols are more stable than lyophilic sols.
(C) Soap forms micelles at any concentration.
(D) Soap forms micelles only above the critical micelle concentration and the Krafft temperature.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working:
Analyze each option:
(A) Colloidal particles are typically larger than pores in ordinary filter paper, so they pass through; thus statement is false.
(B) Lyophobic sols are less stable than lyophilic sols because lyophilic particles have better solvation and aggregation; thus false.
(C) Soap forms micelles only above the critical micelle concentration (CMC); not at any concentration; thus false.
(D) Soap forms micelles only above the CMC and also above the Krafft temperature (the temperature above which micellization occurs for low-solubility surfactants). This statement correctly describes the condition for micelle formation. Hence (D) is correct.
Thus answer is D.

Consider thermodynamic processes occurring in isolated and non-isolated systems.
Which of the following statements about entropy and the second law is/are correct? (One or more options may be correct.)
(A) An irreversible adiabatic process has zero entropy change because q = 0.
(B) In every spontaneous process, the entropy of the system increases.
(C) The entropy of a system can decrease in a spontaneous process if the entropy of the surroundings increases by more.
(D) For an irreversible adiabatic process, the entropy of the system increases even though q = 0.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working:
Analyze each statement.
(A) Irreversible adiabatic process has q=0 but entropy can increase due to irreversibility; entropy change of system not zero generally. So false.
(B) Spontaneous process for isolated system increases total entropy; for non-isolated system system entropy may decrease if surroundings increase more. So false.
(C) In a spontaneous process overall entropy increases; system entropy can decrease if surroundings entropy increase more. This is consistent with second law for non-isolated systems. True.
(D) Irreversible adiabatic process has q=0 but entropy of system increases because irreversibility generates entropy. True.
Thus correct options are C and D.

Thermodynamic systems are classified on the basis of the exchange of energy and matter between the system and its surroundings.
Which one of the following statements about thermodynamic systems is correct?
(A) Water boiling in an open beaker is an example of an open system.
(B) A hot drink in a perfectly insulated, sealed flask is an example of an open system.
(C) A living cell is an example of a closed system.
(D) A gas heated in a sealed rigid steel cylinder is an example of an isolated system.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working:
Thermodynamic systems classification: open (exchange of both energy and matter), closed (exchange of energy only, no matter), isolated (no exchange of either energy or matter). Evaluate each option:
(A) Water boiling in an open beaker: matter (steam) leaves, energy (heat) can leave/enter; thus open system. Correct.
(B) Hot drink in a perfectly insulated, sealed flask: sealed prevents matter exchange; perfectly insulated prevents energy exchange; thus isolated, not open. Incorrect.
(C) Living cell: exchanges both matter (nutrients, waste) and energy (heat, light); thus open, not closed. Incorrect.
(D) Gas heated in a sealed rigid steel cylinder: sealed prevents matter exchange; however heating implies energy input from surroundings, so energy exchange occurs; thus not isolated. Incorrect.
Only statement (A) is correct.

(C) A gas heated in a sealed rigid steel cylinder is an example of a closed system.
(D) Water boiling in an open beaker is an example of a closed system.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working:
Isolated system: no exchange of energy or matter. A hot drink in a perfectly insulated, sealed flask has no heat exchange (insulated) and no matter exchange (sealed), thus isolated. So (A) correct.
Open system: exchanges both energy and matter. A living cell exchanges matter (nutrients, waste) and energy (heat), thus open. So (B) correct.
Closed system: exchanges energy but not matter. A gas heated in a sealed rigid steel cylinder: sealed prevents matter exchange, cylinder rigid but can allow pressure change; heating provides energy exchange, so closed. So (C) correct.
Closed system: exchanges energy but not matter. Water boiling in an open beaker: open beaker allows vapor (matter) to leave, thus open, not closed. So (D) incorrect.
Thus correct statements: A, B, C.
